96	        record=record_index,

123	    with its forward sequence and with its complete IUPAC reverse
124	    complement.  Only candidates whose score is at least *min_score*
125	    survive.  The winner is the highest-scoring candidate; ties are

129	    measured on the original read, and the lexicographically smallest
130	    CIGAR.  On the reverse strand the query interval is converted back to
131	    the original read while the CIGAR stays oriented against the
132	    reference and the reverse-complement read.

151	    )
152	    open_penalty = _score_parameter("gap_open", gap_open, positive=False)
153	    extend_penalty = _score_parameter(

155	    )
156	    if not isinstance(min_score, int) or isinstance(min_score, bool):
157	        kind = type(min_score).__name__
158	        raise ValueError(

160	        )
161	    if min_score < 1:
162	        raise ValueError("min_score must be a positive integer")
163	
164	    reference_records = list(references)
165	    if not reference_records:
166	        raise MappingReferenceError("at least one reference record is required")
167	
168	    def _iter() -> Iterator[ReadMapping]:
169	        for record_index, read in enumerate(reads):
170	            yield _map_one(
171	                record_index,
172	                read,
173	                reference_records,
174	                match,
175	                mismatch,
176	                open_penalty,
177	                extend_penalty,
178	                min_score,
179	            )
180	
181	    return _iter()

184	def _best_candidate(
185	    read: SequenceRecord,
186	    references: list[SequenceRecord],
187	    match: int,
188	    mismatch: int,
189	    gap_open: int,
190	    gap_extend: int,
191	    min_score: int,
192	):
193	    """Return the winning mapping candidate for *read*, or ``None``.
194	
195	    The result is ``(reference_index, alignment, strand)`` where the
196	    alignment on a reverse-strand win is oriented against the read's
197	    reverse complement.  Candidates are scored and tie-broken exactly as
198	    in :func:`map_reads`: highest score, then reference input index,
199	    reference start/end, the forward strand, the original-read query
200	    interval and the lexicographically smallest CIGAR.
201	    """
202	    reverse_record = SequenceRecord(
203	        read.identifier,
204	        _reverse_complement(read.sequence),
205	        read.description,
206	    )
207	    read_length = len(read.sequence)
208	
209	    # The tuple is ordered by the deterministic tie-break rules; the
210	    # smallest tuple wins among equal-score candidates.
211	    best_key: tuple[
212	        int, int, int, int, int, int, int, str
213	    ] | None = None
214	    best_alignment = None
215	    best_strand = ""
216	
217	    for ref_index, reference in enumerate(references):
218	        for strand, query_record in (("+", read), ("-", reverse_record)):
219	            alignment = align_pair(
220	                reference,
221	                query_record,
222	                mode="local",
223	                match_score=match,
224	                mismatch_penalty=mismatch,
225	                gap_open=gap_open,
226	                gap_extend=gap_extend,
227	            )
228	            if alignment.score < min_score:
229	                continue
230	
231	            if strand == "+":
232	                query_start = alignment.query_start
233	                query_end = alignment.query_end
234	                strand_rank = 0
235	            else:
236	                # Convert the interval on the reverse-complement read back
237	                # to zero-based half-open coordinates on the original read.
238	                query_start = read_length - alignment.query_end
239	                query_end = read_length - alignment.query_start
240	                strand_rank = 1
241	
242	            key = (
243	                -alignment.score,
244	                ref_index,
245	                alignment.reference_start,
246	                alignment.reference_end,
247	                strand_rank,
248	                query_start,
249	                query_end,
250	                alignment.cigar,
251	            )
252	            if best_key is None or key < best_key:
253	                best_key = key
254	                best_alignment = alignment
255	                best_strand = strand
256	
257	    if best_alignment is None or best_key is None:
258	        return None
259	    return best_key[1], best_alignment, best_strand
260	
261	
262	def _map_one(
263	    record_index: int,
264	    read: SequenceRecord,
265	    references: list[SequenceRecord],
266	    match: int,
267	    mismatch: int,
268	    gap_open: int,
269	    gap_extend: int,
270	    min_score: int,
271	) -> ReadMapping:
272	    winner = _best_candidate(
273	        read,
274	        references,
275	        match,
276	        mismatch,
277	        gap_open,
278	        gap_extend,
279	        min_score,
280	    )
281	    if winner is None:
282	        return _unmapped(record_index, read)
283	
284	    ref_index, best_alignment, best_strand = winner
285	    read_length = len(read.sequence)
286	    if best_strand == "+":
287	        query_start = best_alignment.query_start
288	        query_end = best_alignment.query_end
289	    else:
290	        query_start = read_length - best_alignment.query_end
291	        query_end = read_length - best_alignment.query_start
292	
293	    return ReadMapping(
294	        record=record_index,
295	        id=read.identifier,
296	        mapped=True,
297	        reference_record=ref_index,
298	        reference=references[ref_index].identifier,
299	        reference_start=best_alignment.reference_start,
300	        reference_end=best_alignment.reference_end,
301	        query_start=query_start,
302	        query_end=query_end,
303	        strand=best_strand,
304	        score=best_alignment.score,
305	        cigar=best_alignment.cigar,
306	    )

"""Deterministic multi-reference mapping of sequencing reads.

Public API:

- :class:`MappingReferenceError` — the reference collection contained no
  records.
- :class:`ReadMapping` — the mapping result for one read: mapped or
  unmapped, with zero-based half-open coordinates and a CIGAR string.
- :func:`map_reads` — align every read against every reference record,
  on both strands, using the local-alignment scoring of
  :func:`~genome_variant.alignment.align_pair`.

Each read is aligned, as given and as its complete IUPAC reverse
complement, against every reference record.  Candidates scoring below
``min_score`` are discarded; the surviving candidate with the highest
score wins, with ties resolved by reference input index, reference
coordinates, strand, original-read query coordinates and CIGAR.  A read
with no qualifying candidate still produces an unmapped result.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass

from .alignment import align_pair, _score_parameter
from .sequence_io import SequenceRecord

__all__ = [
    "MappingReferenceError",
    "ReadMapping",
    "map_reads",
]

# Full IUPAC complementation; the table maps a base to its complement and
# the reversed translation is the reverse complement.
_COMPLEMENT = str.maketrans("ACGTRYSWKMBDHVN", "TGCAYRSWMKVHDBN")


class MappingReferenceError(ValueError):
    """The reference collection contained no reference records."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReadMapping:
    """The mapping of one read.

    For mapped reads ``reference_record`` is the zero-based index of the
    chosen reference in reference input order, ``reference`` its
    identifier, ``reference_start``/``reference_end`` the zero-based
    half-open reference interval, ``query_start``/``query_end`` the
    matching interval on the original read (zero-based, half-open),
    ``strand`` ``"+"`` or ``"-"``, ``score`` the local-alignment score
    and ``cigar`` the CIGAR relative to the aligned strand.  For unmapped
    reads all fields after ``mapped`` except ``record`` and ``id`` are
    ``None``.
    """

    record: int
    id: str
    mapped: bool
    reference_record: int | None
    reference: str | None
    reference_start: int | None
    reference_end: int | None
    query_start: int | None
    query_end: int | None
    strand: str | None
    score: int | None
    cigar: str | None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Return the fixed-order JSON-object representation."""
        return {
            "record": self.record,
            "id": self.id,
            "mapped": self.mapped,
            "reference_record": self.reference_record,
            "reference": self.reference,
            "reference_start": self.reference_start,
            "reference_end": self.reference_end,
            "query_start": self.query_start,
            "query_end": self.query_end,
            "strand": self.strand,
            "score": self.score,
            "cigar": self.cigar,
        }


def _reverse_complement(sequence: str) -> str:
    return sequence.translate(_COMPLEMENT)[::-1]


def _unmapped(record_index: int, read: SequenceRecord) -> ReadMapping:
    return ReadMapping(
        record=record_index,
        id=read.identifier,
        mapped=False,
        reference_record=None,
        reference=None,
        reference_start=None,
        reference_end=None,
        query_start=None,
        query_end=None,
        strand=None,
        score=None,
        cigar=None,
    )


def map_reads(
    references: Iterable[SequenceRecord],
    reads: Iterable[SequenceRecord],
    match_score: int = 2,
    mismatch_penalty: int = 3,
    gap_open: int = 5,
    gap_extend: int = 2,
    min_score: int = 1,
) -> Iterator[ReadMapping]:
    """Map each read against every reference on both strands.

    Every read is locally aligned against every reference record twice:
    with its forward sequence and with its complete IUPAC reverse
    complement.  Only candidates whose score is at least *min_score*
    survive.  The winner is the highest-scoring candidate; ties are
    resolved by, in order, the reference input index,
    ``reference_start``, ``reference_end``, the forward strand (``"+"``)
    over the reverse strand (``"-"``), ``query_start`` and ``query_end``
    measured on the original read, and the lexicographically smallest
    CIGAR.  On the reverse strand the query interval is converted back to
    the original read while the CIGAR stays oriented against the
    reference and the reverse-complement read.

    Reads without a qualifying candidate yield an unmapped
    :class:`ReadMapping`; they are never dropped.  Results are produced in
    read input order and are byte-stable for fixed inputs regardless of
    batching.

    Scoring parameters have the same meaning as for
    :func:`~genome_variant.alignment.align_pair` in local mode;
    *min_score* is a non-boolean positive integer (default 1).  Invalid
    parameters raise :class:`ValueError` before either input is consumed;
    an empty reference collection raises :class:`MappingReferenceError`
    before *reads* is consumed.  Invalid sequence symbols raise
    :class:`~genome_variant.sequence_io.SequenceValidationError` when the
    offending reference or read record is reached.
    """
    match = _score_parameter("match_score", match_score, positive=True)
    mismatch = _score_parameter(
        "mismatch_penalty", mismatch_penalty, positive=False
    )
    open_penalty = _score_parameter("gap_open", gap_open, positive=False)
    extend_penalty = _score_parameter(
        "gap_extend", gap_extend, positive=False
    )
    if not isinstance(min_score, int) or isinstance(min_score, bool):
        kind = type(min_score).__name__
        raise ValueError(
            f"min_score must be a non-boolean integer, not {kind}"
        )
    if min_score < 1:
        raise ValueError("min_score must be a positive integer")

    reference_records = list(references)
    if not reference_records:
        raise MappingReferenceError("at least one reference record is required")

    def _iter() -> Iterator[ReadMapping]:
        for record_index, read in enumerate(reads):
            yield _map_one(
                record_index,
                read,
                reference_records,
                match,
                mismatch,
                open_penalty,
                extend_penalty,
                min_score,
            )

    return _iter()


def _best_candidate(
    read: SequenceRecord,
    references: list[SequenceRecord],
    match: int,
    mismatch: int,
    gap_open: int,
    gap_extend: int,
    min_score: int,
):
    """Return the winning mapping candidate for *read*, or ``None``.

    The result is ``(reference_index, alignment, strand)`` where the
    alignment on a reverse-strand win is oriented against the read's
    reverse complement.  Candidates are scored and tie-broken exactly as
    in :func:`map_reads`: highest score, then reference input index,
    reference start/end, the forward strand, the original-read query
    interval and the lexicographically smallest CIGAR.
    """
    reverse_record = SequenceRecord(
        read.identifier,
        _reverse_complement(read.sequence),
        read.description,
    )
    read_length = len(read.sequence)

    # The tuple is ordered by the deterministic tie-break rules; the
    # smallest tuple wins among equal-score candidates.
    best_key: tuple[
        int, int, int, int, int, int, int, str
    ] | None = None
    best_alignment = None
    best_strand = ""

    for ref_index, reference in enumerate(references):
        for strand, query_record in (("+", read), ("-", reverse_record)):
            alignment = align_pair(
                reference,
                query_record,
                mode="local",
                match_score=match,
                mismatch_penalty=mismatch,
                gap_open=gap_open,
                gap_extend=gap_extend,
            )
            if alignment.score < min_score:
                continue

            if strand == "+":
                query_start = alignment.query_start
                query_end = alignment.query_end
                strand_rank = 0
            else:
                # Convert the interval on the reverse-complement read back
                # to zero-based half-open coordinates on the original read.
                query_start = read_length - alignment.query_end
                query_end = read_length - alignment.query_start
                strand_rank = 1

            key = (
                -alignment.score,
                ref_index,
                alignment.reference_start,
                alignment.reference_end,
                strand_rank,
                query_start,
                query_end,
                alignment.cigar,
            )
            if best_key is None or key < best_key:
                best_key = key
                best_alignment = alignment
                best_strand = strand

    if best_alignment is None or best_key is None:
        return None
    return best_key[1], best_alignment, best_strand


def _map_one(
    record_index: int,
    read: SequenceRecord,
    references: list[SequenceRecord],
    match: int,
    mismatch: int,
    gap_open: int,
    gap_extend: int,
    min_score: int,
) -> ReadMapping:
    winner = _best_candidate(
        read,
        references,
        match,
        mismatch,
        gap_open,
        gap_extend,
        min_score,
    )
    if winner is None:
        return _unmapped(record_index, read)

    ref_index, best_alignment, best_strand = winner
    read_length = len(read.sequence)
    if best_strand == "+":
        query_start = best_alignment.query_start
        query_end = best_alignment.query_end
    else:
        query_start = read_length - best_alignment.query_end
        query_end = read_length - best_alignment.query_start

    return ReadMapping(
        record=record_index,
        id=read.identifier,
        mapped=True,
        reference_record=ref_index,
        reference=references[ref_index].identifier,
        reference_start=best_alignment.reference_start,
        reference_end=best_alignment.reference_end,
        query_start=query_start,
        query_end=query_end,
        strand=best_strand,
        score=best_alignment.score,
        cigar=best_alignment.cigar,
    )

1	"""Single-sample SNV and optional short-indel calling from mapped reads.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	- :class:`VariantCallingError` — the reference or sample configuration is
6	  unusable for calling (empty reference, duplicate reference identifier
7	  or invalid sample name).
8	- :func:`call_variants` — map FASTQ reads with the same local-alignment
9	  scoring, strand search and candidate adjudication as
10	  :func:`~genome_variant.mapping.map_reads`, pile up the quality-filtered
11	  substitution evidence and return a VCFv4.2 document.  Short insertions
12	  and deletions are called additionally when *call_indels* is enabled.
13	
14	By default only substitutions between the bases ``A``, ``C``, ``G`` and
15	``T`` are called.  Insertions, deletions, unaligned portions, unmapped
16	reads and ambiguous bases never contribute substitution evidence.
17	Quality values never participate in mapping; they only filter base
18	evidence.
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import math
24	from collections.abc import Iterable
25	
26	from ._columns import alignment_columns, original_read_position
27	from .mapping import _best_candidate
28	from .quality import ReadQualityError
29	from .sequence_io import SequenceRecord
30	from .vcf import VcfFile, VcfHeader, VcfRecord, normalize_record
31	
32	__all__ = [
33	    "VariantCallingError",
34	    "call_variants",
35	]
36	
37	_ACGT = ("A", "C", "G", "T")
38	_ACGT_SET = frozenset(_ACGT)
39	_PHRED_MIN = 0
40	_PHRED_MAX = 93
41	
42	# One read's normalized indel observations: (pos, ref, alt) mapped to the
43	# reference gaps the event touches and whether its evidence passes the
44	# quality floor.
45	_IndelEventMap = dict[tuple[int, str, str], tuple[frozenset[int], bool]]
46	# One normalized indel candidate: (reference index, pos, ref, alt).
47	_IndelKey = tuple[int, int, str, str]
48	
49	_META_LINES = (
50	    "##fileformat=VCFv4.2",
51	    '##INFO=<ID=DP,Number=1,Type=Integer,Description="Read depth">',
52	    '##INFO=<ID=AC,Number=A,Type=Integer,Description="Allele count">',
53	    '##INFO=<ID=AF,Number=A,Type=Float,Description="Allele frequency">',
54	    '##FORMAT=<ID=GT,Number=1,Type=String,Description="Genotype">',
55	    '##FORMAT=<ID=DP,Number=1,Type=Integer,Description="Read depth">',
56	    '##FORMAT=<ID=AD,Number=R,Type=Integer,Description="Allelic depths">',
57	)

59	
60	class VariantCallingError(ValueError):
61	    """The reference or sample configuration is unusable for calling."""
62	
63	
64	def _quality_threshold(name: str, value: object) -> int:
65	    if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool):
66	        kind = type(value).__name__
67	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-boolean integer, not {kind}")
68	    if not _PHRED_MIN <= value <= _PHRED_MAX:
69	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be between {_PHRED_MIN} and {_PHRED_MAX}")
70	    return value
71	
72	
73	def _positive_threshold(name: str, value: object) -> int:
74	    if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool):
75	        kind = type(value).__name__
76	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-boolean integer, not {kind}")
77	    if value < 1:
78	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive integer")
79	    return value
80	
81	
82	def _fraction_threshold(name: str, value: object) -> float:
83	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
84	        kind = type(value).__name__
85	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a finite number, not {kind}")
86	    fraction = float(value)
87	    if not math.isfinite(fraction):
88	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite")
89	    if not 0.0 <= fraction <= 1.0:
90	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be between 0 and 1")
91	    return fraction
92	
93	
94	def _validate_sample_name(sample_name: object) -> str:
95	    if not isinstance(sample_name, str):
96	        raise VariantCallingError("sample name must be a string")
97	    if not sample_name or sample_name.isspace() or "\t" in sample_name:
98	        raise VariantCallingError(
99	            "sample name must not be empty, whitespace-only or contain tabs"
100	        )
101	    return sample_name
102	
103	
104	def call_variants(
105	    references: Iterable[SequenceRecord],
106	    reads: Iterable[SequenceRecord],
107	    *,
108	    min_base_quality: int = 20,
109	    min_alt_count: int = 2,
110	    min_alt_fraction: float = 0.2,
111	    homozygous_fraction: float = 0.8,
112	    sample_name: str = "SAMPLE",
113	    call_indels: bool = False,
114	    max_indel_length: int = 50,
115	) -> VcfFile:
116	    """Call single-sample SNVs and return them as a :class:`~genome_variant.vcf.VcfFile`.
117	
118	    Each read is mapped exactly as in :func:`~genome_variant.mapping.map_reads`
119	    (same local-alignment scoring, both strands, same candidate
120	    adjudication); unmapped reads contribute nothing.  Every mapped read
121	    contributes at most one observation per covered reference position.
122	    A base is admitted as evidence only when its Phred quality is at least
123	    *min_base_quality* and both the reference base and the observed base
124	    are among ``A``, ``C``, ``G`` and ``T``; on the reverse strand the
125	    quality and base are taken from the corresponding original-read
126	    position.  Insertions, deletions and unaligned alignment columns are
127	    ignored for SNV evidence.
128	
129	    ``DP`` at a position is the total number of admitted ``ACGT``
130	    observations.  The single ALT is the non-reference base with the
131	    highest count (ties resolved in ``A``, ``C``, ``G``, ``T`` order); a
132	    record is emitted only when its count is at least *min_alt_count* and
133	    its share ``AC/DP`` is at least *min_alt_fraction*.  ``GT`` is
134	    ``1/1`` when that share is at least *homozygous_fraction*, otherwise
135	    ``0/1``.  Records follow reference input order and ascending POS.
136	
137	    When *call_indels* is true, short insertions and deletions are called
138	    in addition from the contiguous ``I`` and ``D`` CIGAR segments of each
139	    winning alignment.  An insertion is reported as the left reference
140	    base plus the inserted sequence, a deletion as the left anchor base
141	    plus the deleted reference fragment.  Events without a usable left
142	    anchor, without aligned read bases on both sides, with any relevant
143	    reference or inserted base outside ``ACGT``, or longer than
144	    *max_indel_length* are ignored.  Insertion evidence requires the
145	    flanking and all inserted read bases to meet *min_base_quality*;
146	    deletion evidence requires the flanking read bases to meet it.  Raw
147	    events are minimized and left-aligned with the reference-aware rules
148	    of :func:`~genome_variant.vcf.normalize_record` and equivalent events
149	    are merged by ``CHROM``, ``POS``, ``REF`` and ``ALT``.  An event's
150	    ``DP`` is the number of mapped reads spanning both its flanks with
151	    qualifying flank qualities and no other insertion or deletion at its
152	    boundaries; ``AC`` is the number of those reads supporting the event.
153	    The same *min_alt_count*, *min_alt_fraction* and *homozygous_fraction*
154	    thresholds apply, ``AD`` is ``DP-AC,AC`` and SNV and indel records
155	    are ordered by reference input order, ``POS``, ``REF`` and ``ALT``.
156	
157	    *min_base_quality* is a non-boolean integer in 0-93 (default 20);
158	    *min_alt_count* a non-boolean positive integer (default 2);
159	    *min_alt_fraction* and *homozygous_fraction* finite numbers in 0-1
160	    (defaults 0.2 and 0.8), with the homozygous fraction no smaller than
161	    the minimum ALT fraction; *max_indel_length* a non-boolean positive
162	    integer (default 50).  Invalid thresholds raise :class:`ValueError`
163	    before either input is consumed.  Reads must carry quality values; a
164	    read without them or with a quality/sequence length mismatch raises
165	    :class:`~genome_variant.quality.ReadQualityError` when that read is
166	    reached.  An empty reference collection, duplicate reference
167	    identifiers or an empty/whitespace-only/tab-containing *sample_name*
168	    raise :class:`VariantCallingError`.
169	
170	    *reads* may be any iterable, including one that can be traversed only
171	    once: each read is consumed and mapped exactly once, and resident
172	    memory stays bounded by the reference records, the per-position SNV
173	    counts and the distinct normalized indel candidates — never by the
174	    number of consumed reads.
175	    """
176	    base_quality = _quality_threshold("min_base_quality", min_base_quality)
177	    alt_count = _positive_threshold("min_alt_count", min_alt_count)
178	    alt_fraction = _fraction_threshold("min_alt_fraction", min_alt_fraction)
179	    homo_fraction = _fraction_threshold(
180	        "homozygous_fraction", homozygous_fraction
181	    )
182	    if homo_fraction < alt_fraction:
183	        raise ValueError(
184	            "homozygous_fraction must not be smaller than min_alt_fraction"
185	        )
186	    indel_length = _positive_threshold("max_indel_length", max_indel_length)
187	
188	    sample = _validate_sample_name(sample_name)
189	
190	    reference_records = list(references)
191	    if not reference_records:
192	        raise VariantCallingError("at least one reference record is required")
193	    seen: set[str] = set()
194	    for reference in reference_records:
195	        if reference.identifier in seen:
196	            raise VariantCallingError(
197	                f"duplicate reference identifier {reference.identifier!r}"
198	            )
199	        seen.add(reference.identifier)
200	
201	    # Mapping uses the same local-alignment scoring and candidate
202	    # adjudication as map-reads; callers cannot tune them here.
203	    match, mismatch = 2, 3
204	    open_penalty, extend_penalty, min_score = 5, 2, 1
205	
206	    # One counter table per reference record: position -> [A, C, G, T].
207	    counts_per_reference: list[dict[int, list[int]]] = [
208	        {} for _ in reference_records
209	    ]
210	
211	    # Indel evidence is aggregated read by read (only when enabled), so
212	    # resident memory stays bounded by the reference, the per-position
213	    # SNV counts and the distinct normalized candidates — never by the
214	    # number of consumed reads.
215	    sequences = {
216	        reference.identifier: reference.sequence
217	        for reference in reference_records
218	    }
219	    indels = (
220	        _IndelTracker(
221	            [len(reference.sequence) for reference in reference_records],
222	            base_quality,
223	            indel_length,
224	        )
225	        if call_indels
226	        else None
227	    )
228	
229	    for read in reads:
230	        quality = read.quality
231	        if quality is None:
232	            raise ReadQualityError(
233	                f"record {read.identifier!r}: has no quality values"
234	            )
235	        if len(quality) != len(read.sequence):
236	            raise ReadQualityError(
237	                f"record {read.identifier!r}: quality length {len(quality)} "
238	                f"does not match sequence length {len(read.sequence)}"
239	            )
240	        for score in quality:
241	            if not isinstance(score, int) or not _PHRED_MIN <= score <= _PHRED_MAX:
242	                raise ReadQualityError(
243	                    f"record {read.identifier!r}: quality score {score} is "
244	                    "outside the Phred+33 range 0-93"
245	                )
246	
247	        winner = _best_candidate(
248	            read,
249	            reference_records,
250	            match,
251	            mismatch,
252	            open_penalty,
253	            extend_penalty,
254	            min_score,
255	        )
256	        if winner is None:
257	            continue
258	        ref_index, alignment, strand = winner
259	        columns = alignment_columns(alignment)
260	        _collect_evidence(
261	            read,
262	            quality,
263	            reference_records[ref_index].sequence,
264	            columns,
265	            strand,
266	            base_quality,
267	            counts_per_reference[ref_index],
268	        )
269	        if call_indels:
270	            aligned_at, events = _observe_indels(
271	                read,
272	                quality,
273	                reference_records[ref_index],
274	                columns,
275	                strand,
276	                base_quality,
277	                indel_length,
278	                sequences,
279	            )
280	            assert indels is not None
281	            indels.observe(ref_index, aligned_at, events)
282	
283	    records: list[tuple[int, VcfRecord]] = []
284	    for ref_index, reference in enumerate(reference_records):
285	        chromosome = reference.identifier
286	        reference_sequence = reference.sequence
287	        for position in sorted(counts_per_reference[ref_index]):
288	            counts = counts_per_reference[ref_index][position]
289	            record = _call_position(
290	                chromosome,
291	                reference_sequence,
292	                position,
293	                counts,
294	                alt_count,
295	                alt_fraction,
296	                homo_fraction,
297	            )
298	            if record is not None:
299	                records.append((ref_index, record))
300	
301	    if call_indels:
302	        assert indels is not None
303	        records.extend(
304	            _call_indels(
305	                reference_records,
306	                indels.candidates,
307	                alt_count,
308	                alt_fraction,
309	                homo_fraction,
310	            )
311	        )
312	    # SNV records alone are already produced in this order; the sort only
313	    # interleaves indel records and is stable for equal keys.
314	    records.sort(
315	        key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1].pos, item[1].ref, item[1].alt_text)
316	    )
317	
318	    header = VcfHeader(_META_LINES, (sample,))
319	    return VcfFile(header, tuple(record for _, record in records))
320	
321	
322	def _collect_evidence(
323	    read: SequenceRecord,
324	    quality: tuple[int, ...],
325	    reference_sequence: str,
326	    columns,
327	    strand: str,
328	    min_base_quality: int,
329	    counts: dict[int, list[int]],
330	) -> None:
331	    """Accumulate admitted substitution observations for one read.
332	
333	    Columns carry the single shared interpretation of the winning
334	    alignment; only ``=``/``X`` columns contribute an observation, each
335	    read at most once per reference position.
336	    """
337	    read_length = len(read.sequence)
338	
339	    for column in columns:
340	        if column.op not in ("=", "X"):
341	            # Insertions have no reference position; deletions add no
342	            # base observation; neither contributes SNV evidence.
343	            continue
344	
345	        # The observed base is on the aligned strand, already expressed
346	        # on the reference's forward strand for a reverse-strand win;
347	        # only the quality is mapped back to the original read.
348	        quality_position = original_read_position(column, read_length, strand)
349	        if quality[quality_position] >= min_base_quality:
350	            reference_position = column.reference_position
351	            assert reference_position is not None
352	            observed = column.query_base
353	            reference_base = reference_sequence[reference_position]
354	            assert observed is not None
355	            if observed in _ACGT_SET and reference_base in _ACGT_SET:
356	                table = counts.setdefault(reference_position, [0, 0, 0, 0])
357	                table[_ACGT.index(observed)] += 1
358	
359	
360	def _call_position(
361	    chromosome: str,
362	    reference_sequence: str,
363	    position: int,
364	    counts: list[int],
365	    min_alt_count: int,
366	    min_alt_fraction: float,
367	    homo_fraction: float,
368	) -> VcfRecord | None:
369	    """Build the VCF record for one piled-up position, or ``None``."""
370	    depth = sum(counts)
371	    if depth == 0:
372	        return None
373	
374	    reference_base = reference_sequence[position]
375	    reference_index = _ACGT.index(reference_base)
376	
377	    # Highest non-reference count wins; iterating A, C, G, T in order and
378	    # replacing only on a strict increase resolves ties by that order.
379	    alt_index: int | None = None
380	    alt_observations = 0
381	    for base_index, observed in enumerate(counts):
382	        if base_index == reference_index:
383	            continue
384	        if observed > alt_observations:
385	            alt_observations = observed
386	            alt_index = base_index
387	    if alt_index is None or alt_observations < min_alt_count:
388	        return None
389	
390	    fraction = alt_observations / depth
391	    if fraction < min_alt_fraction:
392	        return None
393	
394	    genotype = "1/1" if fraction >= homo_fraction else "0/1"
395	    reference_observations = counts[reference_index]
396	    info = (
397	        f"DP={depth};AC={alt_observations};AF={fraction:.6f}"
398	    )
399	    sample = (
400	        f"{genotype}:{depth}:{reference_observations},{alt_observations}"
401	    )
402	    return VcfRecord(
403	        chrom=chromosome,
404	        pos=position + 1,
405	        id=".",
406	        ref=reference_base,
407	        alt=(_ACGT[alt_index],),
408	        qual=".",
409	        filter="PASS",
410	        info=info,
411	        format_text="GT:DP:AD",
412	        sample_text=(sample,),
413	    )
414	
415	
416	def _event_gaps(pos: int, ref: str, alt: str) -> frozenset[int]:
417	    """The reference gap positions a normalized event touches.
418	
419	    A gap numbered ``g`` is the boundary between the zero-based reference
420	    positions ``g - 1`` and ``g``.  An insertion touches only its
421	    insertion point; a deletion touches both edges of the deleted
422	    fragment.
423	    """
424	    if len(alt) > len(ref):
425	        return frozenset((pos,))
426	    return frozenset((pos, pos + len(ref) - 1))
427	
428	
429	def _observe_indels(
430	    read: SequenceRecord,
431	    quality: tuple[int, ...],
432	    reference: SequenceRecord,
433	    columns,
434	    strand: str,
435	    min_base_quality: int,
436	    max_indel_length: int,
437	    sequences: dict[str, str],
438	) -> tuple[dict[int, int], _IndelEventMap]:
439	    """Extract one mapped read's indel observations from its alignment.
440	
441	    Returns ``(aligned_at, events)``.  ``aligned_at`` maps a zero-based
442	    reference position to the Phred quality of the read base aligned
443	    there.  ``events`` maps each normalized event key ``(pos, ref, alt)``
444	    (1-based POS) to ``(gaps, quality_ok)``: the reference gap positions
445	    the event touches and whether this read's supporting evidence meets
446	    the quality floor.  A read contributes at most one entry per
447	    normalized event.
448	
449	    The columns use the one shared interpretation of the winning
450	    alignment: their ``boundary`` is the reference gap at the column's
451	    left edge (the consumed position for ``=``/``X``/``D`` and the
452	    insertion point for ``I``).
453	    """
454	    read_length = len(read.sequence)
455	
456	    def column_quality(column) -> int:
457	        index = original_read_position(column, read_length, strand)
458	        return quality[index]
459	
460	    aligned_at: dict[int, int] = {}
461	    for column in columns:
462	        if column.reference_position is not None and column.query_position is not None:
463	            aligned_at[column.reference_position] = column_quality(column)
464	
465	    events: _IndelEventMap = {}
466	    reference_sequence = reference.sequence
467	    column_count = len(columns)
468	    index = 0
469	    while index < column_count:
470	        op = columns[index].op
471	        if op not in ("I", "D"):
472	            index += 1
473	            continue
474	        insertion = op == "I"
475	        # One contiguous I or D CIGAR segment: a maximal run of columns
476	        # gapped on the same side.
477	        start = index
478	        while index < column_count and columns[index].op == op:
479	            index += 1
480	        end = index
481	
482	        length = end - start
483	        if length > max_indel_length:
484	            continue
485	        # The event needs an aligned read base on both sides.
486	        if start == 0 or end == column_count:
487	            continue
488	        if (
489	            columns[start - 1].query_position is None
490	            or columns[end].query_position is None
491	        ):
492	            continue
493	        # The gap sits immediately left of the next reference position;
494	        # the base before it is the left anchor.
495	        gap = columns[start].boundary
496	        anchor = gap - 1
497	        if anchor < 0:
498	            continue
499	        anchor_base = reference_sequence[anchor]
500	        if anchor_base not in _ACGT_SET:
501	            continue
502	        if insertion:
503	            inserted = "".join(
504	                column.query_base or "" for column in columns[start:end]
505	            )
506	            if any(base not in _ACGT_SET for base in inserted):
507	                continue
508	            ref_allele = anchor_base
509	            alt_allele = anchor_base + inserted
510	        else:
511	            deleted = reference_sequence[gap : gap + length]
512	            if any(base not in _ACGT_SET for base in deleted):
513	                continue
514	            ref_allele = reference_sequence[anchor : gap + length]
515	            alt_allele = anchor_base
516	
517	        quality_ok = (
518	            column_quality(columns[start - 1]) >= min_base_quality
519	            and column_quality(columns[end]) >= min_base_quality
520	        )
521	        if quality_ok and insertion:
522	            quality_ok = all(
523	                column_quality(inserted_column) >= min_base_quality
524	                for inserted_column in columns[start:end]
525	            )
526	
527	        # Minimize and left-align with the existing reference-aware
528	        # rules, then merge equivalent events.
529	        raw = VcfRecord(
530	            chrom=reference.identifier,
531	            pos=anchor + 1,
532	            id=".",
533	            ref=ref_allele,
534	            alt=(alt_allele,),
535	            qual=".",
536	            filter="PASS",
537	            info="",
538	        )
539	        normalized = normalize_record(raw, sequences)
540	        key = (normalized.pos, normalized.ref, normalized.alt[0])
541	        gaps = _event_gaps(normalized.pos, normalized.ref, normalized.alt[0])
542	        existing = events.get(key)
543	        if existing is None:
544	            events[key] = (gaps, quality_ok)
545	        else:
546	            events[key] = (existing[0], existing[1] or quality_ok)
547	
548	    return aligned_at, events
549	
550	
551	class _IndelTracker:
552	    """Streaming aggregation of one sample's indel evidence.
553	
554	    Reads are observed one at a time; nothing per read is retained after
555	    :meth:`observe` returns.  Resident state is only:
556	
557	    - ``candidates``: the distinct normalized events observed so far,
558	      mapped to their aggregate ``[gaps, depth, alt_support]``;
559	    - the per-reference aggregates used to backfill the depth of a
560	      candidate that is first observed in a later read.
561	
562	    An event's ``DP`` counts the mapped reads on its reference that span
563	    both flanks (zero-based ``left = pos - 1`` and
564	    ``right = pos - 1 + len(ref)``) with flank qualities of at least
565	    *min_base_quality* and that carry no other event touching the
566	    candidate's gaps.  Because ``right - left = len(ref)`` never exceeds
567	    ``max_indel_length + 1``, the number of reads admitting each flank
568	    pair ``(left, left + distance)`` with ``distance`` up to that bound
569	    is sufficient to reconstruct the spanning count of any candidate
570	    registered later.  Reads carrying an event that touches a gap ``b``
571	    of a future candidate are excluded through three boundary
572	    statistics: counts of reads with an event touching ``b`` that admit
573	    the pair ``(b - 1, b - 1 + distance)`` (``b`` as the candidate's
574	    left gap) or ``(b - distance, b)`` (``b`` as the right gap), and, for
575	    the two-gap deletion case, counts of reads touching both gaps that
576	    admit the pair ``(b1 - 1, b2)`` — combined by inclusion-exclusion
577	    over the at most two gaps of a candidate.  All of these are bounded
578	    by the reference lengths and *max_indel_length*, never by the number
579	    of consumed reads.
580	    """
581	
582	    def __init__(
583	        self,
584	        reference_lengths: list[int],
585	        min_base_quality: int,
586	        max_indel_length: int,
587	    ) -> None:
588	        self._min_base_quality = min_base_quality
589	        # (ref_index, pos, ref, alt) -> [gaps, depth, alt_support].
590	        self.candidates: dict[_IndelKey, list[object]] = {}
591	        # (ref_index, left flank) -> candidate keys registered there.
592	        self._by_left: dict[tuple[int, int], list[_IndelKey]] = {}
593	        # Per reference, left flank -> distance -> reads admitting both.
594	        self._flank_pairs: list[dict[int, dict[int, int]]] = [
595	            {} for _ in reference_lengths
596	        ]
597	        # Per reference, touched gap -> distance -> reads admitting the
598	        # pair (gap - 1, gap - 1 + distance) / (gap - distance, gap).
599	        self._gap_left: list[dict[int, dict[int, int]]] = [
600	            {} for _ in reference_lengths
601	        ]
602	        self._gap_right: list[dict[int, dict[int, int]]] = [
603	            {} for _ in reference_lengths
604	        ]
605	        # Per reference, (first gap, second gap) -> reads touching both
606	        # and admitting the pair (first - 1, second).
607	        self._gap_pairs: list[dict[tuple[int, int], int]] = [
608	            {} for _ in reference_lengths
609	        ]
610	        # Per reference, the largest flank distance a candidate can have:
611	        # len(ref) <= max_indel_length + 1 and both flanks must fit.
612	        self._max_distance = [
613	            min(max_indel_length + 1, max(length - 1, 0))
614	            for length in reference_lengths
615	        ]
616	
617	    def observe(
618	        self,
619	        ref_index: int,
620	        aligned_at: dict[int, int],
621	        events: _IndelEventMap,
622	    ) -> None:
623	        """Fold one mapped read's indel observation into the aggregates.
624	
625	        ``aligned_at`` maps zero-based reference positions to the quality
626	        of the read base aligned there; ``events`` is the read's
627	        normalized event map as produced by :func:`_observe_indels`.
628	        """
629	        admitted = {
630	            position
631	            for position, quality in aligned_at.items()
632	            if quality >= self._min_base_quality
633	        }
634	        max_distance = self._max_distance[ref_index]
635	
636	        # Register newly observed events.  A candidate first observed by
637	        # this read cannot be carried by any earlier read, so its depth
638	        # from earlier reads is the spanning count minus the reads whose
639	        # own events touch the candidate's gaps.
640	        for (pos, ref, alt), (gaps, _quality_ok) in events.items():
641	            key = (ref_index, pos, ref, alt)
642	            if key in self.candidates:
643	                continue
644	            left = pos - 1
645	            distance = len(ref)
646	            depth = self._flank_pairs[ref_index].get(left, {}).get(distance, 0)
647	            touched = sorted(gaps)
648	            blocked = 0
649	            for boundary in touched:
650	                if boundary == left + 1:
651	                    blocked += (
652	                        self._gap_left[ref_index]
653	                        .get(boundary, {})
654	                        .get(distance, 0)
655	                    )
656	                else:  # boundary == left + distance (the right flank gap)
657	                    blocked += (
658	                        self._gap_right[ref_index]
659	                        .get(boundary, {})
660	                        .get(distance, 0)
661	                    )
662	            if len(touched) == 2:
663	                blocked -= self._gap_pairs[ref_index].get(
664	                    (touched[0], touched[1]), 0
665	                )
666	            self.candidates[key] = [gaps, depth - blocked, 0]
667	            self._by_left.setdefault((ref_index, left), []).append(key)
668	
669	        # This read's own contribution to every registered candidate it
670	        # spans: admitted flanks and no other event of this read touching
671	        # the candidate's gaps.
672	        for left in admitted:
673	            for key in self._by_left.get((ref_index, left), ()):
674	                _, pos, ref, alt = key
675	                if pos - 1 + len(ref) not in admitted:
676	                    continue
677	                gaps = self.candidates[key][0]
678	                if any(
679	                    other != (pos, ref, alt)
680	                    and not other_gaps.isdisjoint(gaps)
681	                    for other, (other_gaps, _) in events.items()
682	                ):
683	                    continue
684	                self.candidates[key][1] += 1
685	                evidence = events.get((pos, ref, alt))
686	                if evidence is not None and evidence[1]:
687	                    self.candidates[key][2] += 1
688	
689	        # Fold the read into the aggregates consulted by later
690	        # registrations; only then is this read part of the backfill.
691	        if not max_distance:
692	            return
693	        flank_pairs = self._flank_pairs[ref_index]
694	        for left in admitted:
695	            row = flank_pairs.setdefault(left, {})
696	            for distance in range(1, max_distance + 1):
697	                if left + distance in admitted:
698	                    row[distance] = row.get(distance, 0) + 1
699	        touched = sorted(
700	            {gap for gaps, _ in events.values() for gap in gaps}
701	        )
702	        if not touched:
703	            return
704	        gap_left = self._gap_left[ref_index]
705	        gap_right = self._gap_right[ref_index]
706	        for boundary in touched:
707	            if boundary - 1 in admitted:
708	                row = gap_left.setdefault(boundary, {})
709	                for distance in range(1, max_distance + 1):
710	                    if boundary - 1 + distance in admitted:
711	                        row[distance] = row.get(distance, 0) + 1
712	            if boundary in admitted:
713	                row = gap_right.setdefault(boundary, {})
714	                for distance in range(1, max_distance + 1):
715	                    if boundary - distance in admitted:
716	                        row[distance] = row.get(distance, 0) + 1
717	        gap_pairs = self._gap_pairs[ref_index]
718	        for index, first in enumerate(touched):
719	            if first - 1 not in admitted:
720	                continue
721	            for second in touched[index + 1 :]:
722	                if second - first >= max_distance:
723	                    break
724	                if second in admitted:
725	                    pair = (first, second)
726	                    gap_pairs[pair] = gap_pairs.get(pair, 0) + 1
727	
728	
729	def _call_indels(
730	    reference_records: list[SequenceRecord],
731	    candidates: dict[_IndelKey, list[object]],
732	    min_alt_count: int,
733	    min_alt_fraction: float,
734	    homo_fraction: float,
735	) -> list[tuple[int, VcfRecord]]:
736	    """Build the VCF records for the aggregated indel candidates."""
737	    records: list[tuple[int, VcfRecord]] = []
738	    for (ref_index, pos, ref, alt), (
739	        _gaps,
740	        depth,
741	        alt_support,
742	    ) in candidates.items():
743	        if alt_support < min_alt_count:
744	            continue
745	        fraction = alt_support / depth
746	        if fraction < min_alt_fraction:
747	            continue
748	        genotype = "1/1" if fraction >= homo_fraction else "0/1"
749	        info = f"DP={depth};AC={alt_support};AF={fraction:.6f}"
750	        sample = f"{genotype}:{depth}:{depth - alt_support},{alt_support}"
751	        records.append(
752	            (
753	                ref_index,
754	                VcfRecord(
755	                    chrom=reference_records[ref_index].identifier,
756	                    pos=pos,
757	                    id=".",
758	                    ref=ref,
759	                    alt=(alt,),
760	                    qual=".",
761	                    filter="PASS",
762	                    info=info,
763	                    format_text="GT:DP:AD",
764	                    sample_text=(sample,),
765	                ),
766	            )
767	        )
768	    return records
